stories.title: Scaffold and quality gates
acceptanceCriteria: One npm TypeScript package builds the React client and Hono server
Typecheck, unit test, build, and combined verify commands exist

stories.title: PostgreSQL schema and tenant boundary
acceptanceCriteria: The initial Drizzle migration covers auth, ledger, staging, idempotency, and audit tables
All finance records and queries are scoped to the authenticated user
One tenant cannot read or alter another's records by id, in single or bulk paths, and counter-accounts are per tenant
Schema changes require forward-only data-preserving migrations and preceding-release upgrade tests

stories.title: Multi-tenant local and optional Google auth boundary
acceptanceCriteria: Embedded Better Auth local login is the zero-Google-config default
Google and both modes request openid email profile and refuse to start unless ALLOWED_EMAILS admits somebody
ALLOWED_EMAILS admits exact addresses, whole domains, and * for anyone, and an unset list admits nobody
ALLOWED_EMAILS is applied when an account is created and never as a condition of signing in
One deployment holds many accounts, each seeing only its own ledger, and a linked user can reach one account by local or Google login
Production first-account setup requires a one-time startup code only when the list would refuse the address, and is atomic under concurrency
Zero-environment-variable development uses the real local login through the Vite origin

stories.title: Accounts and categories
acceptanceCriteria: Account and category CRUD use everyday types and optimistic concurrency
In-use records archive and account currency locks after use

stories.title: Transaction engine
acceptanceCriteria: Deposits withdrawals and transfers create correct atomic signed postings
Per-account FX retains sent and received native amounts
CRUD soft delete restore versioning and idempotency are enforced
Explicit-version and fingerprinted all-filter mass edits validate first rebuild postings and commit atomically

stories.title: Transaction browser UI
acceptanceCriteria: Responsive UI provides account and committed transaction CRUD
Liability balances and transaction types use everyday language
Every transaction list supports page and all-matching selection with accessible atomic mass editing

stories.title: Date range and dashboard summary
acceptanceCriteria: Inclusive presets and custom dates persist in URL parameters
Balances and cash flow are grouped per account currency and transfers are excluded

stories.title: Staged transaction workflow
acceptanceCriteria: Staged rows support filters create update selected delete dry-run and commit
Mass commit validates first and changes all rows or none

stories.title: CSV import and export
acceptanceCriteria: Import detects maps previews validates and stages bank CSV
App exports re-import into any account without losing per-account FX amounts, and a transfer asks for its two accounts rather than naming the exporting ledger's

stories.title: MCP OAuth
acceptanceCriteria: Stateless Streamable HTTP MCP is protected by OAuth discovery and PKCE
Read stage and write scopes are least privilege

stories.title: MCP ledger tools
acceptanceCriteria: Discrete tools expose ledger staging summary CSV audit and fingerprint-protected bulk-edit services
Tools return structured content and accurate behavior annotations

stories.title: Audit and security hardening
acceptanceCriteria: Mutations record actor source and before or after values
Cross-tenant IDs cannot be used for reads or writes

stories.title: Production container
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-stage non-root image contains production dependencies app and migrations
Startup migration lock readiness liveness and graceful shutdown work with external PostgreSQL

stories.title: End-to-end acceptance
acceptanceCriteria: Direct staged and MCP-created transactions produce equivalent balances and audit behavior
The production image persists through restart and handles SIGTERM
Ralph dry-run and all quality gates pass

stories.title: Double-entry books and an append-only ledger
acceptanceCriteria: Every transaction settles to zero in each currency it touches, checked before any posting is written
Deposits balance against income, withdrawals against expense, conversions through exchange, and opening balances against equity
Counter-accounts are server-owned, one per kind and currency, and never appear in account lists or pickers
Amount, account, and type corrections reverse the existing postings and write a new set rather than updating or deleting rows
Label-only edits write no postings, and deleted transactions keep theirs while dropping out of balances and reports
Balances, dashboards, and reports derive from postings alone

stories.title: Split transactions
acceptanceCriteria: One transaction divides across several category legs and still settles to zero in each currency it touches
A split cuts the entry's counter-account side into pieces rather than recording the money again, so category totals add up to exactly what left the account
Each leg posts under its own leg id, so a leg's share is attributable wherever spending is reported
Relabelling a leg writes no postings, and changing what a leg is worth writes only the difference
Deleting a split voids the entry a leg at a time
Splits work on committed transactions, on staged rows, and on templates, where the categories are stored and the amounts left blank
A CSV export carries a split by category name and reads back as the same split in another ledger
Mass edit refuses to set a category or a type on a split rather than flattening it, and says why
A transfer cannot be split, having no counter-account side to partition
Reachable over MCP under the same scope rules as everything else

stories.title: Recurring transactions
acceptanceCriteria: A recurrence names a shape, its accounts, an optional amount, a schedule, and policies for month length and weekends
Daily, weekly, monthly and yearly schedules, every N of those, on a day of the month or on a relative day such as the second Tuesday or the last Friday
On its due date it writes an ordinary staged row, and never a posting
A recurrence that has never run and one that ran and was discarded are distinguishable, so a silent scheduler is visible rather than inferred
Catch-up after downtime proposes each missed occurrence once, and running the scheduler twice for the same occurrence proposes it once
Generated rows carry no bank import reference, and are dated their occurrence rather than the day the scheduler happened to run
A recurrence naming an account or category that no longer resolves proposes the row anyway, flagged, rather than failing silently
Deleting a recurrence leaves rows already proposed or committed untouched
Nothing is ever proposed dated before the day the recurrence was created
The scheduler runs inside the server process and is on by default, so the single container deployment needs nothing added, and an environment flag hands the job to a separate container
One replica proposes at a time under a session advisory lock, and a per-occurrence unique key refuses a duplicate even if the lock is bypassed
Reachable over MCP under the same scope rules as everything else

stories.title: Reporting
acceptanceCriteria: Net worth over a range, per currency, derived from postings alone, with no figure spanning currencies anywhere in the reply
Income against expense over a range, agreeing with the dashboard's cash flow for the same range and accounts
Category trends over time, spanning income as well as expense, agreeing with the existing spending-by-category figures and ranking for a single period
A cash flow statement over the accounts money can be spent from, decomposed by the class of the account on the far side of each transaction, reconciling to the change in those accounts
A balance sheet as of one date, and a trial balance that totals zero in every currency at every date, archived accounts included
A per-account register listing every posting with the balance before and after it, opening on the balance the window starts from and closing on the one it ends on
Every figure stops at today in the person's own timezone, and a range that has not happened yet reports nothing rather than today's figures
A row's total is the sum of its buckets where they are movements and the balance it closes on where they are balances
Archived accounts are included or excluded consistently across every report, with a closed account contributing the zero it actually holds
The range, the report and the grouping live in the URL, as the range does elsewhere
Every report is reachable over MCP as a read tool, and every figure drawn in a chart is also present as text

stories.title: Budgeting
acceptanceCriteria: A standing budget covers every period in its window, so an ongoing budget is one row and nothing materialises the periods nobody has reached
An amount set for one period overrides the standing budget for that period alone, and the report says which of the two produced each figure
Windows for one category, period unit and currency may not overlap, so what a past period intended survives a later change
Spending is compared against the limit on the same period grid the reports bucket by, computed from postings alone
A category budgeted and never spent on still appears, rather than being dropped as a zero
A refund lowers the category it came back to, because spending is summed signed and the counter-account carries the direction
Splits attribute each leg to its own category, and transfers contribute nothing, both without a rule of their own
Nothing in this story writes a posting, and deleting a budget changes no balance and no report
Deleting or archiving a category leaves no orphaned budget, and a budget is never a reason a category cannot be deleted
Every figure stops at today in the person's own timezone, and the day used is reported
No figure spans currencies anywhere in the reply
Reachable over MCP, reads on ledger:read and writes on ledger:write, with the browser and an agent calling the same services

stories.title: Rollover and sinking funds
acceptanceCriteria: A budget can carry what a period did not spend into the next one, and an overspend forward as a debt against it
A cap holds the carry inside a number in both directions, so neither a fund nobody draws on nor a debt nobody repays runs away
A sinking fund names an amount and a date and works out each period's own figure from what is still needed and how many periods are left
Nothing is stored per period: every carried figure is folded at read time from the plans, entries and postings that were already there
Two budgets with a gap between them are two budgets, and no carry crosses the gap
The fold is bounded, and a report that hit the bound says so rather than reporting a carry that started from nothing part way through
Reachable over MCP and from the browser on the same fields, and a budget that carries nothing reports exactly what it did before
